primitives.name: Spatial Rim Pattern Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using over 22 million shots captured in high-­‐resolution by Noahlytics, we reveal previously hidden systematic biases in entry left-­‐right and entry depth from all positions on the court.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_R': 'Left-Right deviation in inches', 'D': 'Entry depth in feet', 'S': 'Shot success rate'}
primitives.assumptions: Shots are captured with consistent sensor accuracy; spatial distribution reflects true biomechanical tendencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When L_R or D exceed 4 standard deviations from mean, systematic bias becomes statistically significant.

layer2.mapping: Maps spatial shot data to probabilistic skill ranking via kernel density estimation of shot trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Heat map variance across court positions

primitives.name: Machine Learning Shooter Ranking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then, we focus on the high-­‐resolution shot data from 509 NBA, college and high school players to train a machine-­‐learning algorithm that predicts shooting ability from 25-­‐shot sessions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{skill}': 'Predicted shooter skill level', 'N_{shots}': 'Number of shots in session (25)', 'A_{accuracy}': 'Accuracy score derived from ML model'}
primitives.assumptions: Training data is representative of diverse skill levels; 25-shot sessions provide sufficient statistical power.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N_shots < 10, model performance degrades due to insufficient data for generalization.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between raw shot features and predicted skill scores via supervised classification.

primitives.name: Systematic Bias Quantification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Previously we could only expose low percentage shooting from different areas of the court, while now we can explore why shooters miss from those positions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B_{LR}': 'Left-Right systematic bias in inches', 'B_{D}': 'Depth systematic bias in feet', 'P_{loss}': 'Expected shooting percentage loss due to bias'}
primitives.assumptions: Bias is consistent across repeated attempts from same court position; statistical significance threshold set at p < 0.05.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Bias becomes negligible when B_LR < 1 inch and B_D < 0.5 feet.

layer2.mapping: Kernel-based estimation of bias-induced shooting loss using empirical shot trajectory distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage reduction in shooting accuracy under biased conditions

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in leveraging high-resolution shot capture to extract latent patterns in shooter behavior, specifically Left-Right and Depth biases. These biases are modeled as systematic deviations from optimal shot trajectories, which can be quantified using spatial heat maps derived from millions of shots. The introduction of machine learning algorithms allows for prediction of shooter skill from short sessions, improving upon traditional metrics like shooting percentage that suffer from small-sample noise. The mathematical framework integrates statistical inference with spatial pattern recognition, enabling a dual approach: one that identifies where errors occur (via heat maps) and another that predicts future performance (via ML models). Failure modes include overfitting in small samples and misinterpretation of spatial trends without proper normalization. The system's robustness depends on maintaining consistent sensor calibration and ensuring representative training data across skill levels.
